mentions.name: MCPGuard
mentions.description: MCPGuard is a CLI tool that audits MCP (Model Context Protocol) configurations for plaintext credentials and migrates them into the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Linux SecretService, Windows Credential Manager). Its `mcpguard audit` command finds exposed API keys, and `mcpguard migrate` moves them to the OS keychain, replacing real keys in the config file with vault references so credentials never touch disk again. Installable via `npm install -g mcpguard-cli`.
mentions.problem: API keys for services like GitHub, Linear, and Notion sit in plaintext in ~/.config/claude/claude_desktop_config.json, so anyone with read access to that file (malicious MCP server, compromised dependency, RCE) gets all the keys instantly.
mentions.source_excerpt:
MCPGuard fixes this: it scans your MCP configs, detects plaintext credentials, 
and migrates them to your OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Linux SecretService, 
Windows Credential Manager).

  $ mcpguard audit   # finds exposed keys
  $ mcpguard migrate # moves them to OS keychain

Your config file then has vault references instead of real keys. 
The credentials never touch disk again.
